turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with Mrs. Iyer from Nagpur?

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Yes, this is she. Who is calling please?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I am Ananya from the City Police Community Outreach cell, and I am calling to provide a security awareness update for senior citizens.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Police? Oh my goodness, has something happened to my family?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No no, please do not worry, everything is fine. I am just calling to warn you about a fake lottery scam going around your neighborhood.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: A lottery? I have not entered any lottery, why are they targeting me?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: They target many people, often claiming you won twenty five thousand rupees to lure you into giving your bank details.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Twenty five thousand is a lot of money. What do I do if they call me?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Just remember that the police and banks will never ask for your OTP, PIN, or Aadhaar number over the phone.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I see. But what if they say they are from my own bank?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Even then, never share your password or OTP with anyone, because no official officer will ever demand those details.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Thank you for telling me, beta. I will be very careful now.
